newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields up, taking cautious view.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields up, taking cautious view.

text.p: *Australian bond yields rose in a slow session with market players reluctant to chance their hand ahead of a speech by RBA governor Macfarlane, U.S. jobs and a long holiday weekend.
*No key local data until next week.
Australian bond yields rose in a slow session on Thursday with market players reluctant to chance their hand ahead of several key events.

The mildly heavy tone was triggered by U.S. Treasuries ending a four day run of gains and speculative selling emerged when there was no word on policy from the Reserve Bank in the wake of Wednesday's GDP data.

There had been talk of a rate cut in offshore trading hours, but in the event the central bank was silent and the market is hopeful that it might now get a feel on policy thinking when governor Ian Macfarlane delivers a speech in London later today.
Macfarland is due to speak to a Westpac conference at 1.50 a.m. (1550 GMT), although the market will be reluctant to get too carried away by what he says.

"He could say one thing, and then do exactly the opposite,' said one trader, referring to Macfarlane's comments on May 8 that there was no economic gain from a further rate cut. The RBA cut rates by 50 basis points 15 days later.

The local subdued tone also reflects caution ahead of Friday's key non-farm payrolls data, with the Federal Reserve still viewed with having a tightening bias, and as Australia has a local holiday on Monday.

The market generally underperforms against the dollar bloc, notably against the short-end of the New Zealand curve, despite quarterly N.Z. private sector wages rising a slightly stronger than expected 1.1 percent. The local yield curve flattened in the absence of a RBA monetary policy announcement.
